hints: Count the horizontal distance on the c.r.o. between the emitted peak and the reflected peak using the $1\,\text{cm}$ scale - it is $3\,\text{cm}$.
The $6.3\,\mu\text{s}$ given is only transmitter to reflector, so the time between the two peaks on the trace is out plus back.
Time-base in $\mu\text{s cm}^{-1}$ is total time between peaks divided by horizontal separation in $\text{cm}$.
walkthrough: Measure the peak-to-peak separation on the trace. With the $1\,\text{cm}$ grid, the emitted peak and reflected peak are $3.0\,\text{cm}$ apart horizontally.
State the physics: the time between the two peaks is the round-trip time of the pulse. Time-base $= \text{time} / \text{horizontal distance}$.
Divide by the screen distance to get the time-base: $\text{time-base} = 12.6\,\mu\text{s} / 3.0\,\text{cm} = 4.2\,\mu\text{s cm}^{-1}$ with correct units.

options.A: This divides only the one-way $6.3\,\mu\text{s}$ by $3\,\text{cm}$, forgetting the reflected pulse has travelled out and back.
options.B: This is close to dividing the round-trip time by about $4\,\text{cm}$ instead of the measured $3\,\text{cm}$ separation of the two peaks.
options.C: The $12.6\,\mu\text{s}$ round trip spread over $3.0\,\text{cm}$ gives $12.6/3.0 = 4.2\,\mu\text{s cm}^{-1}$.
options.D: This uses the one-way $6.3\,\mu\text{s}$ as if it were the time between the emitted and reflected peaks on the screen.
